governing_rules: eArc stores artefacts and provenance; it does not canonize, ratify, approve, endorse, select, deprecate or establish truth.
Source-declared claims are preserved as source claims and are never adopted as eArc authority.
A directory name, path, filename, index entry, manifest entry or checksum does not confer authority.
Source objects, ingestion events, archive records, derivatives, observations and interpretations remain distinct.

examples.source_declared_status: may be CANONICAL in its originating QH256 or publication context if that source says so
examples.earc_assessment: NOT_ASSESSED unless a specific eArc observation exists

examples.example: legacy file containing a canonical K501 declaration

examples.source_declared_status: as declared by source; otherwise UNKNOWN
examples.earc_assessment: STATIC_OBSERVATION only when a specific code review is recorded

canonical/.interpretation: directory name retained for historical path identity only; contents are archived development artefacts

relationship_to_external_authority: External canonical status may be recorded as a source claim/reference; eArc neither grants nor revokes it.
append_only_correction: Add new dated metadata observations; never silently rewrite source bytes or erase earlier claims.
